rules.title: Compact density
rules.description: Use a compact layout density with more content per screen.
rules.rationale: Chinese homepages show about three times the visual density and nearly twice the main content blocks; NN/G reports Chinese users prefer relatively high information density and perceive complexity through familiarity. It fires only when the measured page is sparser than the midpoint between the two sample means, so pages that are already dense are left alone.

evidence.summary: Measured higher visual density and more blocks on Chinese homepages, plus reported user tolerance for density.

sources.locator: Section 2.2 table: visual density 38.21 vs 12.87; main content blocks 5.91 vs 3.14
sources.supports: Higher density and more blocks on Chinese homepages

sources.locator: Section 'Yes, Chinese Sites Are Often Complex': Chinese participants tolerated complexity and appreciated density, especially on portal and news sites (n=6 Chinese users, 12 total)
sources.supports: Chinese participants prefer fairly high information density (small qualitative study)

gaps: Sample is institutional (municipal) homepages; commercial sites are not covered.
NN/G is small (6 Chinese users): Chinese users also met many usability problems on complex sites and some designs were judged too complicated.
Chinese users were less accepting of the simple sites tested, but this is not a test of this transformation.

Delta-based: the density threshold (25.54) is the midpoint of two sample means from a study of municipal homepages. It is provisional and compared against our own metric definition, whose scale may differ from the study's. Replace with own measurements (A2).

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.
Touch targets must stay usable.
Does nothing on pages already at or above the threshold; also does nothing if the page could not be measured.

history.change: Dimension and pole assigned and versioning started (B18). Content unchanged from rule set 0.3.0; earlier changes are in the git history.

rules.title: Tight spacing scale
rules.rationale: The literature review reports less dominant white space on Chinese sites, consistent with denser layouts; doc 01 section 3.3 lists white space as less dominant.

evidence.summary: Review of 17 studies reports more elements and less white space on Chinese sites.

sources.locator: Section 2.1: Chinese sites have more elements and interactions; Western sites more white space
sources.supports: Less white space in Chinese designs

sources.locator: Section 3.3 table: white space less dominant

gaps: Methods and definitions differ across the reviewed studies.
No test of whether tighter spacing helps users.

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.

history.change: Dimension and pole assigned and versioning started (B18). Content unchanged from rule set 0.3.0; earlier changes are in the git history.

rules.title: Vivid palette
rules.description: Increase colour saturation for a livelier look.
rules.rationale: The 2026 study finds Chinese palettes wider, more saturated and brighter, and the 2022 review reports more red and blue. Doc 02 warns against the red+gold stereotype, so this rule changes saturation only, not hue.

evidence.summary: Two independent sources report more saturated, brighter, wider palettes on Chinese sites.

sources.locator: Section 2.2 other results: Chinese palettes wider, more saturated, brighter
Section 2.1: more red and blue on Chinese sites

gaps: Evidence comes from institutional (municipal) homepages; commercial sites are not covered.
No evidence that raising saturation improves experience.
Hue is deliberately untouched.

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.
Must keep text contrast at or above WCAG AA.
Never apply a red/gold stereotype.

history.change: Dimension and pole assigned and versioning started (B18). Content unchanged from rule set 0.3.0; earlier changes are in the git history.

rules.title: Image-led cards
rules.description: Give images more prominence in cards.
rules.rationale: The 2026 study measures higher image diversity (6.32 vs 4.34) and visual density on Chinese homepages. Extending this to product and feed cards is an extrapolation from institutional homepages, so the level is emerging.

evidence.summary: Higher image diversity and visual density measured on Chinese homepages; card-level use is untested.

sources.locator: Section 2.2 table: image diversity 6.32 vs 4.34; visual density 38.21 vs 12.87

gaps: Evidence comes from institutional (municipal) homepages; commercial sites are not covered.
Product and feed cards are not covered by the evidence.
evidence.validationPlan: Internal before/after review (B8) on the paired test sites; add real-user testing after V1.

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.
Images must keep alt text.

history.change: Dimension and pole assigned and versioning started (B18). Content unchanged from rule set 0.3.0; earlier changes are in the git history.

rules.title: Flat hierarchy
rules.description: Present many parallel entry points at similar weight.
rules.rationale: Chinese homepages show more main content blocks (5.91 vs 3.14) and the project synthesis describes hierarchy as distributed across modules rather than absent (doc 02). The link between block count and flat visual weight is interpretive.

evidence.summary: More main content blocks measured; distributed hierarchy described in synthesis.

sources.locator: Section 2.2 table: main content blocks 5.91 vs 3.14
docs/02 visual level: hierarchy distributed across modules

gaps: Block count does not directly measure visual weight.
Evidence comes from institutional (municipal) homepages; commercial sites are not covered.
evidence.validationPlan: Internal before/after review (B8) on the paired test sites; add real-user testing after V1.

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.
Distributed hierarchy is not absence of hierarchy; keep headings and semantics intact.

history.change: Dimension and pole assigned and versioning started (B18). Content unchanged from rule set 0.3.0; earlier changes are in the git history.

evidence.summary: More posters/infographics measured; banners described as numerous and dynamic.

sources.locator: Section 3.3 table: banners numerous and dynamic

gaps: Evidence comes from institutional (municipal) homepages; commercial sites are not covered.
Posters and infographics are not the same as commercial promotion banners.
evidence.validationPlan: Internal before/after review (B8) on the paired test sites; add real-user testing after V1.

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.
Does not add or invent promotions.

evidence.validationPlan: Internal before/after review (B8) on the paired test sites; add real-user testing after V1.

rules.title: Discovery feed prominence

gaps: No study cited that tests this transformation.
Platform observation is mostly of apps, not websites.
evidence.validationPlan: Internal before/after review (B8) on the paired test sites; add real-user testing after V1.

limits: Tendency from research, not a universal rule; varies by site and sector.
Only if a recommendations area is detected.

rules.title: Recommendations higher on home
rules.description: Move recommendations just below the hero on home pages.
rules.rationale: Builds on the observed centrality of feeds in Chinese homepages. The specific reordering has no direct evidence, so it remains a hypothesis.

evidence.summary: Feed centrality is observed; the proposed position is a design guess.

sources.locator: Section 3.3 table: feed can be central to the homepage

gaps: The specific position has no evidence.
Reordering may break expected flow on some sites.
evidence.validationPlan: Verify in B6 that the original order is fully recoverable and that the page still works; internal before/after review.

limits: Structural; needs component recognition (B5).
Must keep original order recoverable.

rules.title: Shortcut strip near the top
rules.description: Show a small strip of links to sections that already exist in the main navigation, just above the hero block.
rules.rationale: Chinese homepages show more main content blocks (5.91 vs 3.14 in Li 2026), which suggests more parallel entry points. A strip of links to existing sections makes several entry points reachable near the top without moving or removing anything; that it helps users is a design hypothesis.

evidence.summary: More main content blocks measured on Chinese homepages; the shortcut strip is a design guess based on that observation.

sources.locator: Section 2.2 table: main content blocks 5.91 vs 3.14
sources.supports: More parallel content blocks on Chinese homepages

gaps: Evidence comes from institutional (municipal) homepages; commercial sites are not covered.
No evidence that a shortcut strip improves findability.
Duplicated links add content; may be redundant where the navigation is already visible.
evidence.validationPlan: Internal before/after review on Baidu, Taobao and Bilibili homepages: strip appears only when 3+ safe links exist, original page restores exactly; later check with real users (deferred, decision #8).

limits: Copies at most 6 existing links (text and address only); never creates new destinations.
Skipped when fewer than 3 usable links are found.

history.change: Dimension and pole assigned and versioning started (B18). Content unchanged from rule set 0.3.0; earlier changes are in the git history.
